preconditions.description: The first line of input is a single integer t (1 ≤ t ≤ 1000) representing the number of test cases.

preconditions.expression: all(2 <= int(line) <= 300000 for line in stdin.split() if line.isdigit() and int(line) >= 2)
preconditions.description: For each test case, the first line is an integer n (2 ≤ n ≤ 300000) representing the number of rooms.

preconditions.expression: all(len(s) == n for n, s in zip([int(line) for line in stdin.split() if line.isdigit()], [line.strip() for line in stdin.split() if not line.isdigit()]))
preconditions.description: For each test case, the second line is a string s of length n, where each character is '<', '>', or '-', representing the state of the conveyor belts.

preconditions.expression: all(c in ['<', '>', '-'] for s in [line.strip() for line in stdin.split() if not line.isdigit()] for c in s)
preconditions.description: Each character in s is either '<' (anticlockwise), '>' (clockwise), or '-' (off).

postconditions.expression: all(stdout.strip().isdigit() for stdout in [line.strip() for line in stdin.split() if not line.isdigit() and line.strip() != ''])
postconditions.description: For each test case, the output is a single integer representing the number of returnable rooms.

postconditions.expression: all(0 <= int(stdout.strip()) <= n for n, stdout in zip([int(line) for line in stdin.split() if line.isdigit()], [line.strip() for line in stdin.split() if not line.isdigit() and line.strip() != '']))
postconditions.description: The output integer for each test case is between 0 and n (inclusive), representing the count of returnable rooms.

postconditions.expression: all(any('\n'.join([str(count) for count in [int(stdout.strip()) for stdout in [line.strip() for line in stdin.split() if not line.isdigit() and line.strip() != '']]]) == '\n'.join([str(count) for count in expected_counts]) for expected_counts in [compute_expected_counts(stdin)]) if (lambda: (stdin := ''.join(stdin.split())))() else False)
postconditions.description: For each test case, the output count of returnable rooms is correct, where a room i is returnable if there exists a path from i to i that leaves and returns to i using the conveyor belts. The path must not be trivial (i.e., the snake must leave the room and return later).
